notes.title: Battle Pass Season 20: “Flying Dragon” and Its Warbond Shop!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/cdeee69cf7845740c389edaf54113aeee5180dfd.jpg[/img]

Meet Battle Pass Season 20, named Flying Dragon! This season, we’ve lined up interesting Chinese-themed decals and decorations, plus the Chinese premium WZ-141-1, a unique light tank featuring two 105 mm recoilless guns. There’s also the handy Dutch SB-25J for France, capable in both air and ground battles. And as always, there’s warbonds, decals, boosters, Silver Lions, premium account time, wagers and more!

Additionally, make sure to check out the Warbond shop, running in parallel with this Battle Pass season. We’ve added a decoration trophy, USSR tanker profile icons and the unique “Lady Death” pinup decal. All details below!

[quote][b]Beginning on:[/b] July 23rd (12:00 GMT)
[b]Ending on:[/b] October 22nd (12:00 GMT)[/quote]

[i][b]What is the Battle Pass?[/b]
The Battle Pass is an event that lasts for 90 days where players can earn rewards for completing challenges and earning progress points. Rewards range from Silver Lions and boosters to season-exclusive decals, decorations, vehicles and more. Completing the Battle Pass is simple: you earn progress points that unlock levels, earning valuable things along the way!
[url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/battlepass/196-battle-pass-seasons]Check out the Wiki here to learn more[/url].[/i]

[i][b]Leveling up the Battle Pass & Challenges[/b]
Leveling up is simple! Gather progress points to unlock more levels. One level is 10 progress points. Points can be obtained through logging into the game, completing Daily Tasks and completing specific Challenges. New Battle Pass Challenges unlock once a week and another three can be obtained through reaching specific levels.
[list]
[*] [b]Login to the game![/b] Get 1 to 5 progress points for doing this.
[*] [b]Complete Daily Tasks![/b] Get 2 to 5 progress points for each of these.
[*] [b]Complete Battle Pass Challenges![/b] Get 30 points for each of these.
[/list][/i]

[url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/battlepass/bp_20_season style=button]Click here for all of the Challenges[/url]

[h2]Rewards in Season 20[/h2]
Purchasing the Battle Pass for 2,000 Golden Eagles will allow you to access every level. Purchasing the improved version for 2,500 Golden Eagles comes with an extra 150 progress points (15 levels from the get go). 

Not got enough time to complete the Battle Pass? You can purchase progress points for Golden Eagles 28 days after the season begins.

[quote]The Battle Pass can be accessed on the right side of the screen while in the hangar.[/quote]

[url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/battlepass/bp_20_season style=button]Click here for all of the Rewards[/url]

Check out all of the rewards in the season below.

[h2]New vehicles this season[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/2c0650697df275b60f7c8aba48f1a50542d28872.png[/img]
[h2]WZ-141-1 (China)[/h2]
[h3]A Premium Light Tank for China at Rank IV[/h3]

The WZ-141 prototype was developed in China in an attempt to create a light, air-droppable tank destroyer similar to the American M50 Ontos and Japanese Type 60. The vehicle’s tracked platform has bulletproof armor, and its main armament consists of two 105 mm recoilless guns. Development of the vehicle began in 1976, with the WZ-141-1 test model ready the following year. Despite successful testing, the WZ-141 was never accepted into production. In the game, the WZ-141-1 will be a mobile, compact and maneuverable tank destroyer with powerful weapons, allowing it to hide and ambush enemies. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/5ef10bf2b785ac2dbd900291902facc20d1ab5f5.png[/img]
[h2]SB-25J (France)[/h2]
[h3]A Premium Bomber for France at Rank III[/h3]

American B-25 Mitchell bombers were not only used by the United States, but were actively supplied to Allied nations during the Second World War. A notable foreign operator of this plane was the Netherlands, who used the B-25 primarily in the Pacific theater. The SB-25J variant features eight large-caliber machine guns in the nose and four on the sides of the cockpit, giving this plane a combined total of 12 guns. The SB-25J also has excellent defensive armament and a good bomb load. In the game, this versatile medium bomber can operate effectively in both Air and Ground battles.  

[h2]Decals, Decorations and a Profile Icon[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/ae45ea4a94bb458e6d82eb52134a431b8fb6c5bc.png[/img]
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [td][b]“Emblem of the 84th Brigade”[/b] decal[/td]
        [td][b]“Emblem of the Special Forces of the Nanjing Military Region”[/b] decal[/td]  
        [td][b]“Emblem of Special Forces Brigade of the 71st Army Group”[/b] decal[/td]
        [td][b]“Emblem of the 4th Airborne Forces Company”[/b] decal[/td]  
    [/tr]
[/table]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/c00c6552dfdc92793936059d0e349c4c2b94b657.png[/img]
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
 [td][b]“Automatic grenade launcher (China)”[/b] decoration[/td]  
        [td][b]“Type 64”[/b] decoration[/td]
        [td][b]“MLRS (China)”[/b] decoration[/td]
        [td][b]“Chinese paratrooper”[/b] profile icon[/td]
    [/tr]
[/table]


[h2]Battle Trophy with Past Vehicles[/h2]
Missed out on previous Battle Pass vehicles? The Battle Trophy has you covered, featuring four vehicles from past Battle Passes or events. Opening this trophy will give you one vehicle from the list. If you have them all, you’ll instead receive Silver Lions and the special “Golden Battles Wager”, allowing you to earn up to 1,000 Golden Eagles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/8edeeb2774b64254ebe1ac13ebcf0ce1c34355a6.png[/img]
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [td][b]HMS Cadiz[/b][/td]
        [td][b]LCM(6) Zippo[/b][/td]  
    [/tr]
[/table]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/04a0d0c1d51c4a2b60144dc915f942d298c09715.png[/img]
[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [td][b]Turan II[/b][/td]
        [td][b]VL Myrsky II[/b][/td]  
    [/tr]
[/table]

[h2]Get Silver Lions, Consumables, Premium Account Time and More in the Battle Pass![/h2]
The Battle Pass doesn’t just feature decals, decorations and vehicles, it also contains a lot of other useful items. This includes a large amount of Silver Lions, Warbonds to spend in the Warbond shop, Orders, Wagers and Backups for use in battles, a Test Drive for one of the new vehicles before you get it, 10 days of Premium Account time, unique camouflages for the two new vehicles and a title and loading screen to remember your accomplishments. 

[h2]Get the next Battle Pass for free with Upgrade Coupons![/h2]
Two “Upgrade Coupons” are at levels 105 and 125 in the Battle Pass and are both needed to get the next Battle Pass for free. They also make the two new vehicles tradable on the Gaijin Market if you prefer. 

[quote]To purchase a Battle Pass using the “Upgrade Coupon”, you need to wait until the current season ends and the new season begins. You’ll then be able to exchange two Upgrade Coupons in the Battle Pass purchase window. Upgrade Coupons must be available in your inventory to do this. [/quote]

[h2]The Warbond Shop in Season 20![/h2]
Check out some of the main Warbond shop items in Season 20! You can view the full list of items available as well as the conditions for receiving them in-game.

[quote]The Warbond shop can be accessed by clicking on Shop > Warbond Shop from the hangar or from the Battle Pass window by clicking “Shop”[/quote]

[i][b]What is the Warbond Shop?[/b]
The Warbond shop is connected with and runs in tandem with the Battle Pass. Items in the Warbond shop can be purchased with a currency called Warbonds that are earned in the Battle Pass. There are a total of 6 shop levels and each one can be unlocked by reaching specific levels in the Battle Pass. In addition to purchasing with Warbonds, each item from shop level 3 requires a certain number of medals to purchase. Medals can be obtained through completing Special Tasks. [/i]

[h2]Vehicles[/h2]

[h3]Aigle (France)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/b3e42e317c6942de60ed446545bc73223a2c1447.png[/img]
Aigle features five main turrets with a single 138.6 mm gun in each, capable of firing HE or SAPBC. This Destroyer also has six torpedoes, an array of machine guns, and a 71 km/h top speed, making Aigle a good all-round Destroyer, capable of taking out a range of enemies.

[h3]Mörkö-Morane (Sweden)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/4eff9e06d11d66b294cfa5464f9917305c06bb53.png[/img]
The Mörkö-Morane is a Finnish variant of the French M.S.406, delivered in 1940. This variant features a single 12.7 mm machine gun or 20 mm cannon in the nose (swappable via modifications), one 7.5 mm machine gun on each wing, a good top speed of over 500 km/h and an excellent turn time.

[h3]Grant I (USA)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/824bc99e663553863dcc31e821df7d77887e830e.png[/img]
The Grant I was derived from Britain needing a tank, they opted for the M3 Medium and modified it to their needs. This tank features two cannons; a fast-firing 37 mm gun in a conventional turret — which features significantly more armor than the Lee variant, along with a 75 mm at the side of the hull, firing the same powerful APHE shell as the early Shermans.

[h3]Z47 (Germany)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/ec71b6120e69d03777d1359a090dfdcd0730d282.png[/img]
The Type C Z47 was developed due to the shortcomings of the Type A and B. Featuring three main turrets with two 12.8 cm guns in each, the Z47 packs a punch against other enemy Destroyers. This ship also features twelve torpedoes and several 2 cm and 3.7 cm anti-aircraft guns.

[h3]Mustang Mk IA (Great Britain)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/768d69af69f2ebd25e10dd189eb26cc5412bf32e.png[/img]
The Mustang Mk IA is a British variant of the classic American P-51. It features several unique camouflages, four 20 mm Hispano cannons that can deal heavy damage to enemy aircraft and great flight performance. It lacks suspended weaponry options, but the AP rounds fired by its cannons can tear through the top of enemy tanks with ease.

[h3]T-34-57 (1943) (USSR)[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/812853b3b7a64e25f822bcc0dcbe8b788fc21367.png[/img]
The T-34-57 (1943) was a late, experimental variant of the T-34, featuring the 57 mm ZIS-4M cannon in a modified hexagonal turret. It combines workable armor with effective mobility and a powerful cannon, with both high penetration and a very fast reload.

[h2]Decals[/h2]
Season 20 returns a Trophy with tiger decals, plus the new Lady Death decal, continuing this themed series!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/c84ce96fced2e96a1d23252b1a2428d30c7faab7.png[/img]
[b]“Lady Death”[/b] pinup decal
[h2]Trophies[/h2]
Like decorating your ground vehicles? Then check out the Road signs trophy, featuring several road signs for your vehicles! Prefer making your player profile unique? Open the profile icon trophy to get yourself a USSR tanker! 

[h2]Consumables[/h2]
Alongside trophies, vehicles and decals are a bunch of useful consumable items, including boosters, universal backups, wagers & orders, premium vehicle rentals and talismans — all perfect for helping you through the game.

[b]Get out there and get yourself some goodies![/b]

notes.title: Update 2.47.0.63
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/9ff301e250ed0fd31f8a32757224181271497bf9.png"][/img]
[/p][h2]Ground Vehicles[/h2][list][*][p]A bug that caused shells to ricochet through the armor in some cases at high impact angles has been fixed. ([b][url="https://community.gaijin.net/issues/p/warthunder/i/lEtG954f6lyU"]Report[/url][/b]).[/p][/*][*][p]A bug that caused the calculations of hits on crew members to take impact angle into account has been fixed. notes.title: It’s fixed! №106
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/247237204632c6915be20d903c2acc24900f88d7.jpg[/img]

Today, we’ve rounded up and will be going over some of the bug fixes and improvements that we’ve made to the game today and over the past few weeks. If you’d like to catch up on every fixed bug, then be sure to check out [url=https://warthunder.com/en/game/changelog/]the changelog section on our website[/url].

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/236390/discussions/3/594028005822702867/]Feel free to leave your feedback on this update here[/url]

If you’ve found a bug that you’d like to report, you can do so on our [url=https://community.gaijin.net/issues/p/warthunder]community bug reporting platform[/url].

[h2]Issues after the major[/h2]
The release of the major update unfortunately came with some unforeseen and complicated problems, with the team working effectively around the clock to get them resolved as soon as possible. We always try to identify as many issues during internal testing and the dev server with the help of the community, but as War Thunder is a very technical and complex game with lots of interconnecting parts, it isn’t always possible to catch everything. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/6d215e56f331828b0de3e1d59f2f5053e6aed535.jpg[/img]

We’re starting this edition of It’s Fixed with key issues that we corrected after the launch of the major update. For aircraft, certain planes sometimes would be unable to move on runways, damage from air-to-air missiles and SAMs, as well as HE shells fired at aircraft were calculated incorrectly, and missiles could lose their target for no apparent reason. On the ground, allied and enemy vehicles sometimes moved jerkily, and some maps had collision issues.

All these bugs have already been fixed, and we want to elaborate on one of them in more detail and explain a little bit what happened. One of the main problems that many players faced at top ranks, unstable damage with missiles, is a manifestation of a bug related to the incorrect position of explosions when calculating hits on aircraft. This extrapolation error has occurred only in online battles and not consistently, so despite the fact that the erroneous code appeared on the open dev server and stayed there for about a week, we were unable to detect the bug due to its unstable reproduction. And although the first significant fix in the damage model, which was able to compensate for many manifestations of this bug, was uploaded to the main server after 24 hours, we were able to find the root of the problem and fix it only after 6 days. We apologize for any inconvenience experienced in the parts of the game that were affected, and thank you for your understanding.

[h2]Pinned weapons selector[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/aa001fbb93cf6c8f2cac294333af4f010e60b701.jpg[/img]

Now onto new additions. We’ve introduced the ability to pin the weapons selector in air battles. This gives players the ability to interact with the selector directly, similar to the action panel elements. The aircraft can still be controlled by mouse movements, and by holding down the corresponding key (on PC, this key is Alt), you display the cursor. With the cursor you can press on the missiles, bombs or countermeasures that you want. This is more convenient and faster than constantly turning the selector on and off and shows the remaining countermeasure amount clearly. In the future, we plan to add an indication of which hardpoint the next launch or drop will be from. This menu expands and collapses with one click, so be sure to try it! 

[h2]Radar Control Screen Target Filter[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/088482493361d24408454ec48f4d18bbeb9f660d.jpg[/img]

The Leviathans major update introduced a new Radar Control Screen interface for anti-aircraft vehicles. In today’s update, we’ve added the ability to set a filter in the target list. You can now see all air targets, or only enemies, or only allies. This makes things more convenient when the sky is teeming with contacts! We plan to add a few more filter options by target type soon.
 
[h2]TV Seeker Improvements[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f18fb1e557a3a2bfefe52fc1081543ce06c1fa98.jpg[/img]

A couple of pleasant changes were made to missiles with a TV homing head. The picture when viewed from these types of missiles now has more contrast. It is similar to how missiles see their targets in reality, and allows players to distinguish targets more clearly. When capturing a target in third-person view, the icon now differs depending on the captured target (in this case a crosshair is displayed in the square), or if it’s just a point on the ground (in this case the icon looks like an empty square).

[h2]That’s not all[/h2]
Check out the full list of fixes and improvements in the update notes below! Here’s some snippets to pique your interest: Multi-Vehicle SAM System launchers now correctly spawn into arches and tunnels, the destruction of launchers no longer reduces the counter of remaining respawns, and battleship hulls no longer receive excessive damage from high-explosive shells.


[h3]Recent updates:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/236390/announcements/detail/547864982714322869]Update 2.47.0.46[/url]

[/list]

[h2]Today's Update 2.47.0.47:[/h2]
[h2]Aircraft[/h2]
[list]
[*] The CEP (Circular error probable) for munitions with GNSS guidance has been reduced according to the known data.
[*] [b]A-10C[/b] — the ability to simultaneously use a targeting pod and the AGM-65D missiles on TER launchers with 3 missiles has been added. ([url=https://community.gaijin.net/issues/p/warthunder/i/CydO2aLlTWtk]Report[/url]).
[*] [b]Hunter FGA.9[/b] — the position of the drop-tanks has been corrected so that the drop-tanks and air-to-air missiles can be used together.
[*] A bug that made it possible to destroy the nuclear bomb and therefore make it explode before it hit the ground has been fixed.
[*] [b]Ka-29[/b] — a bug that caused no change in the helicopter’s performance characteristics when equipping the external 30 mm 2A42 cannon has been fixed.

[*] [b]Mirage IIIS C.70 (Germany)[/b] — a bug that made it impossible to jettison the drop-tanks if a booster or conformal fuel tank was installed has been fixed. ([url=https://community.gaijin.net/issues/p/warthunder/i/2FIkoxUL6mKW]Report[/url]).

[*] [b]MiG-23MLD[/b] — the intermediate position of the wing sweep in the automatic sweep control mode has been changed to 33 degrees at medium speeds. 
[b]Source:[/b] [i]“Инструкция лётчику самолета-истребителя МИГ-23МЛ. Техническое описание”.[/i]
[*] [b]MiG-17PF (Italy), Lim-5P[/b] — engine name has been corrected to VK-1F. 
[b]Source:[/b]  [i]“Самолёт МиГ-17П с двигателем ВК-1Ф. Техническое описание. Книга 1. Лётные характеристики самолёта”, 1954.[/i]
[*] [b]MiG-17PF (Italy), Shenyang F-5, Lim-5P[/b] — engine mass in X-ray has been increased from 892 kg to 990 kg. 
[b]Source:[/b] [i]“Авиационный турбореактивный двигатель ВК-1Ф. Описание конструкции”.[/i]
[/list]
[h2]Ground Vehicles[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]MSC[/b] — the increased durability of the side screens has been reduced. A bug where the armor element near the sight did not form fragments when penetrated has been fixed. 
[*] [b]SPYDER AIO[/b] — Python 5 rocket engine has been replaced with a reduced smoke motor. ([url=https://community.gaijin.net/issues/p/warthunder/i/aYoKgiH6vo64]Report[/url]).
[*] [b]CS/SA5, IRIS-T SLM, SPYDER AIO, EldE 98[/b] — mistakenly present recoil from missile launches has been removed.
[/list]
[h2]Locations and Missions[/h2]
[list]
[*] In variants of the missions below where the Battle Rating of the session is 10.7+, an air spawn point has been added:
[list]
[*] [b][Operation] Spain[/b]
[*] [b][Operation] Vietnam[/b]
[*] [b][Operation] Moscow[/b]
[*] [b][Operation] Sinai[/b]
[/list]
[*] [b]Test Site-2271[/b] — enemy detection zones around spawn points have been increased to make it harder for enemies to remain undetected while behind a spawn point.
[/list]
[h2]Interface[/h2]
[list]
[*] In 3rd person view, the target acquisition mark for AGM seekers now differs depending on whether the seeker has acquired a point on the ground or a target. Target acquisition is still displayed as a square with a crosshair, and acquisition of a point on the ground is displayed as a square without a crosshair.
[*] A bug where the service record search bar did not work if the query contained capital letters has been fixed. ([url=https://community.gaijin.net/issues/p/warthunder/i/ca5w6RbM9RuW]Report[/url]).
[*] When using a gamepad, the cursor will now return to the selected game mode after closing the server selection window.
[/list]
[h2]Graphics[/h2]
[list]
[*] The picture in the form of a TV missile seeker has been made more contrasting, which makes it more realistic, and the details in it more distinguishable.
[*] A bug where enemy aircraft “contacts” became more transparent and disappeared at shorter distances than before the 2.47 Leviathans update has been fixed. ([url=https://community.gaijin.net/issues/p/warthunder/i/Ju1vFZNRaOY4]Report[/url]).
[/list]
[hr][/hr]
[i]Patch notes reflect only key changes, meaning they may not include a complete list of all improvements made. Additionally, War Thunder is constantly being updated and some changes may not require an update. Changes reflected in patch notes are formed by taking reactions and requests of the community from the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fcommunity.gaijin.net%2Fissues%2Fp%2Fwarthunder]bug reporting service[/url], forums and other official platforms into account. Bug fixes and changes are implemented in order of importance, for example a game-breaking bug will be worked on and implemented sooner.[/i]

notes.title: Graphics Improvements in the Leviathans Update!
notes.content:
With the Leviathans major update, we have some good news for those who like playing with the latest graphics technologies on display. Ray tracing has improved a lot since the last update and today we wanted to share with you what to expect!

[h2]First up, performance[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/34edf05bf830b359b8d5808a03033e0f7c4fa818.jpg[/img]

We’re always working to make performance better and come up with ways to lessen the load on the CPU and GPU for a smoother experience.

On the GPU side, we’ve come up with some ideas on improving performance in the most demanding scenario for Ray tracing, such as rendering foliage. Tracing rays through trees and forests is a time consuming task for the GPU. By changing the method of how rays are checked against leaves and branches, we were able to avoid severe performance degradation in these cases. Driving through a forest, or flying close to one while looking at it is much smoother now.

And those who have the hardware for it can expect it to be even better soon, as Microsoft announced a technique called Opacity Micro Maps (OMM) to be part of DirectX. This will be another bigger jump in tracing foliage. Microsoft also announced that Shader Execution Reordering is coming to DirectX which will help with performance in general. These features are in preview in DirectX and we are working on utilizing them to make performance even better.

Ray tracing is not only a GPU intensive workload, but also very demanding on the CPU, as we constantly need to update the acceleration structures to keep the Ray tracing in sync with the world. On the CPU side, we have identified many bottlenecks that were limiting performance. Ray tracing is using up to 8 CPU cores to do its work, and we have worked on faster processing and better synchronization on those cores. The gains here depend on many factors (CPU type, RAM speed, etc.) but every system should see a performance improvement.

[h2]Next, image quality[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/3ea2d1c25ba68d6be654d87a7597f3facdca3b81.jpg[/img]

It’s important to keep the game visuals improving. Ray tracing already improves shadows, reflections and ambient occlusion. But now it is time to improve global illumination.

There’s a new option now, which when enabled, replaces ambient occlusion. We call it Path Traced Global Illumination or PTGI. Back in 2018 (time flies) when we introduced Global Illumination (GI) to the game it was a big visual leap, but technology keeps improving and now we can do it even better.

PTGI is simulating light, bouncing around in the scene, and calculates the lighting on surfaces which are indirectly lit. For example, in shadows, indoors or valleys. The old GI does a great job with this very topic, but it has its limitations. It works on a much more simple and inaccurate representation of the world, and it has a limited range.

The first usually shows as light leaking. This is when light appears where it should not be. As on the floor here on the left.

PTGI cleans all of these leaks up and makes the lighting in interior areas much more consistent with the rest of the scene. Also as you can see, PTGI embraces light more as it can simulate its bounces on a larger scale.

[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/e85fed9bd4c21f38d53742425726a2a368b9b7f9.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/766a705ab675b9ebfa5fb9e059b05ee4ea0ed2ed.jpg"][/img][/carousel]
[b](1) PTGI Off | (2) PTGI On[/b]

The limited range is sometimes very obvious. For example, during ground battles on a map with cloudy weather or in large indoor areas. The line in the middle of the bus stop is the edge of the area covered by the old GI system.

With PTGI, this limitation is gone, and the entire image is receiving consistent global lighting.

[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/60c776a4b325b3fe13a51f1e66ed02ec1d6afa33.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/45f4cf107c4785e2ca37f6a0679175e49a1e49b3.jpg"][/img][/carousel]
[b](1) PTGI Off | (2) PTGI On[/b]

Another very notable difference is that as the old GI is working on a simplified scene, many times it thinks the surface should be lit by the sky, when it shouldn’t. As a result, the indirectly lit areas having a blue tint on them — more than there should be.

As PTGI is working with the actual scene, and simulate more light bounces, the area is lit more naturally.

[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/b8dbe9ab0eec0ae6c80bf0b885a027ac5e460595.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/944b369463eae3cea25334026184fd7c2e0f9863.jpg"][/img][/carousel]
[b](1) PTGI Off | (2) PTGI On[/b]

The same can be seen on more open areas as well. With the old GI, the tiles and pavement have a somewhat unnatural blue color on them.

PTGI now simulates this more correctly and results in a more consistent image.

[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/137544b7fc13e09d67199c74a96ef17f563c92f9.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f705d2e743efbfcfcc6440731f919afac354cad0.jpg"][/img][/carousel]
[b](1) PTGI Off | (2) PTGI On[/b]

[h2]Finally, you may have downloaded some extra FPS[/h2]
With the Leviathans update, when your GPU supports it, you can enable Frame Generation (FG). We have three flavors of it:
[list]
[*] NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation, working on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 40 Series and above GPUs when DLSS is enabled
[*] AMD FSR Frame Generation, working on AMD Radeon RX 5000 Series and above, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 Series and above and Intel Arc, when FSR is enabled
[*] Intel XeSS Frame Generation, working on Intel Arc GPUs when XeSS is enabled
[/list]
Depending on the method and your hardware, the GPU can generate one to three frames for every rendered frame. This will result in a higher perceived FPS. The gain is dependent on many components of your system, but note that it is very rare that one generated frame for every normal frame would double your frame rate.

The best case for it to work, is when you have a high refresh rate monitor, like 120 Hz, and an already high FPS close to the monitor’s frequency, like around 100. In a case like this, FG can help you reach the refresh rate of the display.

NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation is using NVIDIA REFLEX to reduce the latency. For the other vendors, we also added support for Intel XeLL and AMD Radeon Anti Lag 2. These are similar to REFLEX, and in the options menu, you see the option for the technology applicable to your hardware. If you are using an AMD GPU, you will see Anti Lag 2 for example.

Note that FG and latency reduction is independent from Ray tracing, so you can use it without Ray tracing as well, but most of these technologies only work with DX12.

So what is the final performance you ask? It depends on many factors of your system, but you should see an uplift. To have a sense of the current performance on Ray tracing, here you can see the game running on Movie graphics preset, Medium RT preset (featuring all RT effects, even PTGI), XeSS anti-aliasing with Balanced upscaling on an MSI Claw 8 gaming handheld. 

[previewyoutube=at5bO9-lNNE;full][/previewyoutube]

As you can see the game is easily running at 70-90 FPS on a handheld like this.

And last but not least, we’re still working on the final touches to Ray tracing for consoles. Soon you’ll be able to try it yourself.

notes.title: Update 2.47.0.46
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/2651e93193f651994995523a28ac921ec553633d.png[/img]

[h2]Aircraft[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]F-2A, F-2A ADTW, Su-34[/b] — gating (filtering) restrictions for speed and range when switching from TWS mode to track modes have been made more stringent in order to reduce the likelihood of acquiring the wrong target.
[/list]
[h2]Interface[/h2]
[list]
[*] The ability to pin the visual weapon selector to the screen using an action in its interface has been added. 
[list]
[*] The pinned selector does not stop aircraft control when moving the cursor. Interaction with it is performed using the cursor activated using the “Show mouse cursor” action. 
[*] The pinned selector can be collapsed and expanded using the “Visual weapon selector” action, and the pinned state is remembered just in the battle you are in.
[/list]
[*] The ability to filter the list of targets by allied/enemy team has been added to the radar control screen.
[*] A bug where turning on sight stabilization on aircraft via the gamepad radial menu also turned on the night vision device has been fixed.
[/list]
[h2]Locations and Missions[/h2]
[list]
[*] In variants of the missions below where the Battle Rating session is 10.7+,  an air spawn point has been added:
[list]
[*] [b][Operation] Afghanistan[/b]
[*] [b][Operation] Kamchatka[/b]
[*] [b][Operation] Smolensk[/b]
[*] [b][Operation] Golan Heights[/b]
[*] [b][Operation] Denmark[/b]
[/list]
[*] [b]Finland[/b] — a bug that could cause invisible collision to appear in some places in the location has been fixed. Missions in this location have been returned to the rotation. 
[/list]
[h2]Graphics[/h2]
[list]
[*] A bug where when PTGI (Path Traced Global Illumination) was enabled, unused ambient occlusion in the final scene would still be rendered, negatively impacting performance, has been fixed. 
[/list]
[h2]Sound[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]T54E1, T54E2[/b] — engine sound has been replaced with the more appropriate M4A3 engine sound.
[/list]

notes.title: Decals and Discounts on Rare Vehicles for US Independence Day!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/3184ccb3bff71861a2eb0aab4eb018fd7ffcc2df.png[/img]

Happy 4th July! On July 4th 1776, the Declaration of Independence of the United States was officially adopted by the Second Continental Congress. The anniversary of this event is the United States’ national holiday, celebrated with fireworks, parades and speeches throughout the country.

[h3]The P-38K, F-86F-35 and M26E1 are temporarily available at a 30% discount for Golden Eagles![/h3]
The following are available at a 30% discount:

[list]
[*] M26E1 (rank IV) for 5236 Golden Eagles
[*] F-86F-35 (rank V) for 6489 Golden Eagles
[*] P-38K (rank IV) for 3416 Golden Eagles!
[/list]

[quote][b]When:[/b] When: From July 4th (11:00 GMT) until July 7th (11:00 GMT).
[b]Where:[/b] USA > Aviation / Army > Premium vehicles.[/quote]

[b]About this aircraft[/b]
[list]
[*] The M26E1 retains the medium profile of the M26 Pershing, but instead features the T54 90 mm gun, giving it Super Pershing firepower!
[*] The F-86F-35 Sabre features the Skyblazers aerobatic team camouflage. It can quickly gain speed and maintains excellent maneuverability. For air combat, it is armed with six 12.7 mm machine guns, and for attacking ground targets, it can take up to two 1000 lb bombs or 16 HVAR rockets.
[*] The P-38K is essentially a P-38G with more powerful V-1710-75/77 engines producing over 1600 HP. Thanks to these engines along with improved propellers, the P-38K surpasses all other aircraft in its family in terms of flight performance. For firepower, the P-38K features a 20 mm cannon and four 12.7 mm machine guns concentrated in the nose, with an ammunition count of 2,000 rounds!
[/list]

[h3]Get the “US Independence Day 2025” decal![/h3]
This decal is available for this special day!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/648b1c92ac810b6c6e90acf5973f1d48e13c2fa8.png[/img]
[b]“US Independence Day 2025”[/b] decal

[quote][b]When:[/b] From July 4th (11:00 GMT) until July 7th (11:00 GMT).
[b]Task:[/b] Play 3 battles using US vehicles at rank III or higher to receive the “US Independence Day 2025” decal.

[b]Additional details:[/b]
[list]
[*] Your activity must not be below 70%.
[*] You can complete the task in random battles, except for [Assault] mode.
[*] Track your progress in the hangar by clicking Nickname → Achievements → Holidays → US Independence Day.
[*] You can find the decal in the “Holidays” tab in the customization menu.
[/list][/quote]

notes.title: A Decal and Discounts on the J29D and J35A for Swedish Air Force Day!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/0c6ed966b5613a86938adb025b277d2682f47b42.jpg[/img]

Swedish company Bofors, with a history dating back to 1646, is one of the oldest arms manufacturers in the world. In 1937, it founded its Saab division to build aircraft for the Swedish Air Force, which became a separate branch of the armed forces on July 1st, 1926. Saab has produced thousands of aircraft, including some of Sweden’s most famous ones. 

[h3]The J29D and J35A are temporarily available for Golden Eagles with a 30% discount![/h3]
The J29D (rank V) is available for 6237 Golden Eagles, and the J35A (rank VI) for 6363!

[quote][b]When:[/b] From July 1st (11:00 GMT) until July 4th (11:00 GMT).
[b]Where:[/b] Sweden > Aviation > Premium vehicles.[/quote]

[b]About these jet aircraft[/b]
[list]
[*] The [url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/J29D]J29D Tunnan[/url] is an experimental modification of the first Swedish jet fighter. It features excellent speed, four powerful cannons and a wide range of rockets for attacking ground targets. Choose for yourself what role to play in battle!
[/list]
[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/48a79de2a65fc00851dbbbf6fccfb021b157dc4d.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/35b703c3846be932142b3007f149d7634826ed70.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/738facf33cc27bf76355f83cb905c04068f53dc6.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/9b6c41312b1740ae03dc8915faf16e39e9f474b6.jpg"][/img][/carousel]
[list]
[*] The [url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/J35A]J35A Draken[/url] is a plane for real aces. It has no countermeasures, so you’re going to have to dodge enemy missiles the old fashioned way. The J35A has excellent speed and maneuverability, and is a master of turning combat. In addition to two cannons, it can carry up to four guided air-to-air missiles. 
[/list]
[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/d69cdb351a27cd078e49087f6f4dcfb8d3349c5e.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/93ce6ce60bb12e38b8e3ba2d480015beb2db3ca4.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/d9991835f3b4610491f8d4cc1b18c4b4e08be078.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/31871897ddd8d52e9e96b09d350c8492f1e71243.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/f295e90e0e97be5811285bb401b94e02090acb9b.jpg"][/img][/carousel]

[h3]Get the “Helicopter wing patch” decal![/h3]
This decal is available for this special day!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/bbaca5c17bb4ea52ff51c6cfe612bbb489905bdd.png[/img]
[b]“Helicopter wing patch”[/b] decal

[quote][b]When:[/b] From July 1st (09:00 GMT) until July 4th (09:00 GMT)
[b]Task:[/b] Play 3 battles using Swedish aircraft at rank III or higher to receive the “Helicopter wing patch” decal.

[b]Additional details:[/b]
[list]
[*] Your activity must not be below 70%.
[*] You can complete the task in random battles, except for Enduring Confrontation missions, and [Assault] mode.
[*] Track your progress in the hangar by clicking Nickname → Achievements → Holidays → Swedish Air Force Day.
[*] You can find the decal in the “Sweden → Aircraft” tab in the Customization menu.
[/list][/quote]

notes.title: A Decal and Discounts on Japanese Vehicles for Japan Self-Defense Forces Day!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/84b4fb2ab7e542dcdda793e43f54817113445027.jpg[/img]

On July 1st, 1954, the modern Japan Self-Defense Forces were founded. Today, they are ready to defend the homeland from any threats, participate in international missions and help civilians in emergency situations, which happen often in Japan. More than 250,000 people serve in the Japan Self-Defense Forces, and the country continues to develop modern military equipment. 

[h3]The IJN Kiyoshimo, J2M4 Kai and Type 74 (G) are temporarily available for Golden Eagles with a 30% discount![/h3]
The following are available at a 30% discount: IJN Kiyoshimo (rank III) can be picked up for 3416 Golden Eagles, J2M4 Kai (rank IV) for 2695 and Type 74 (G) (rank VI) for 6111.

[quote][b]When:[/b] From July 1st (09:00 GMT) until July 4th (09:00 GMT).
[b]Where:[/b] Japan > Bluewater fleet / Aviation / Army > Premium vehicles.[/quote]

[b]About each of these vehicles[/b]
[list]
[*] [url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/IJN_Kiyoshimo]IJN Kiyoshimo[/url] is well suited to protect allies from air attacks and destroy more fragile targets. Her air armament is represented by a huge number of autocannons, although her main caliber guns only have access to high-explosive shells. IJN Kiyoshimo also features sixteen 610 mm torpedoes. 
[/list]
[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/a86c67da4414832f309f2b0f47d6a9832589b41d.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/3373079e82ac504654a1bd062dd521599bd129cd.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/a88f47953571f41ae143010ee0c9bdc3e18b5987.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/a79733e5f639d1f381de37e03e46a8c649a76469.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/60f3eeb8f4212b7702dd46b77fd64d85c38efa25.jpg"][/img][/carousel]
[list]
[*] The [url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/J2M4_Kai]J2M4 Kai[/url] features a 1854 HP engine, allowing it to outperform its predecessors in speed and rate of climb and perform well at high altitudes. Its four 20 mm cannons are excellent against enemy aircraft. 
[/list]
[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/7112b68e150f731a3a3112302c749dcac1bd39f9.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/da70d77cbdc91a1e3c25c49a00bc002517b1745f.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/54c1975e85a4c3631e773cba79a73da4ce4f0032.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/19705a578c8d4da1320bbcf3c97f0ab5d5cd90cc.jpg"][/img][/carousel]
[list]
[*] The [url=https://wiki.warthunder.com/unit/jp_type_74_mod_g_kai]Type 74 (G)[/url] is the most advanced modification of the Type 74 MBT of the Japanese Self-Defense Forces. Its main weapon is the 105 L7A3 gun with a two-plane stabilzer. It’s also equipped with a thermal imager for the gunner, a laser rangefinder and a laser warning system! 
[/list]
[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/19c5e6149cafab1eab971da1463e92faa61346bc.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/c01d6a3ae0ee258eab3e75f167f19d6e79ed42b5.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/69bf14009a27ecd47e803eec9d7e965d843262ee.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/6ef6789ffa586bc2bb465ae36932f9bb37a2354e.jpg"][/img][/carousel]

This decal is available for this day!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/16874dcd4f75ca521f3ca46f0a7af14cf21b3fd6.png[/img]
[b]“Armor Battalion Flag”[/b] decal

[quote][b]When:[/b] From July 1st (09:00 GMT) until July 4th (09:00 GMT).

[b]Task:[/b] Play 3 battles using Japanese vehicles at rank III or higher to receive the “Armor Battalion Flag” decal.

[b]Additional details:[/b]
[list]
[*] Your activity must not be below 70%.
[*] You can complete the task in random battles, except for Enduring Confrontation missions, and [Assault] mode.
[*] Track your progress in the hangar by clicking Nickname → Achievements → Holidays → Japan Self-Defense Forces Day.

notes.title: A Themed Decal for British Armed Forces Day!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/3607c4be94a3dc1f305e14981a38f20db7906fc8.jpg[/img]

On the last Saturday in June, Great Britain celebrates its military — both current soldiers and veterans, with the reservists celebrating their day three days earlier. There are 170 events across the country, from parades and performances to family and charity events. The aim of the day is to show public support for the country’s armed forces. 

[h2]Get the “British Armed Forces Day 2025” decal![/h2]
We’ve created this British-themed decal for this day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/45261f4b7b46f1743cca4ce2fbec2c8bf2615d03.png[/img]
[b]“British Armed Forces Day 2025”[/b] decal

[b]When:[/b] From June 27th (12:00 GMT) until June 30th (12:00 GMT).
[b]Task:[/b] Play 3 battles using British vehicles at rank III or higher to receive the “British Armed Forces Day 2025” decal.

[b]Additional details:[/b]
[list]
[*] Your activity must not be below 70%.
[*] You can complete the task in random battles, except for Enduring Confrontation missions, and [Assault] mode.
[*] Track your progress in the hangar by clicking Nickname → Achievements → Holidays → British Armed Forces Day.
[*] You can find the decal in the “Britain → Tanks” tab in the Customization menu.	
[/list]

notes.title: Meet the “Leviathans” Major Update!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/1c372cf774e2823612815daa6f0d8ca737b27d64.jpg[/img]

[h3]Meet Leviathans, War Thunder’s second major update of 2025![/h3]

Leviathans introduces several new vehicles to the game. The Japanese F-2A, the Swiss subtree, Czechoslovakia’s first domestic aircraft and the renowned RAH-66 Comanche! Ground forces benefit from the new Multi-Vehicle SAM system mechanic, enabling control of up to three vehicles at once. Battleship fans can rejoice with the most famous naval powerhouses in the world, such as Yamato and Bismarck, now making their way into the game. The Falkland Islands map is now available in Air Battles, and Berlin and Kuban have undergone visual enhancements. Alongside these additions, we’ve added fuel dumping, improved graphical effects and Frame Generation, made UI refinements, added new mechanics, and improved numerous aspects of the game!  

[h3]Check out the changelog to see all the fixes, vehicles and other features that we’ve included in this major update.[/h3]

[previewyoutube=VyTslTfRrDM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/236390/discussions/0/594026878893837571/]Please feel free to leave your feedback on this major update in the feedback thread here.[/url][/h3]

[h2]Ground Vehicles: New SAMs, Second World War Premium Packs, the Badger IFV and Leclerc MSC![/h2]

Check out these premium packs for the USA, USSR and Great Britain, each featuring three vehicles. Each pack forms the backbone of a solid lineup, particularly as each one has an SPAA. Plus, they’re decked out with some cool looks, including camouflage netting.

[h3]Second World War Premium Packs[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/39ca08ce89c775a68cb95ea67ecf54b16237240d.png[/img]

New SAM vehicles have been added for several nations. Some of them feature the new Multi-Vehicle SAM system mechanic (more on how that works in the dedicated section below), plus new missiles. 

Here we have the EldE 98 for Sweden and CLAWS for the USA, with the latter being a Multi-Vehicle SAM System capable of firing the AIM-120 and AIM-9X!

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [td][h3]EldE 98[/h3][/td] 
        [td][h3]CLAWS[/h3][/td] 
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/20e401affdf86d03434c4eeb9c9708ac4a6072aa.jpg[/img][/td] 
        [td][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/e68cd3d6fd1de7759c83fce2a7847bc2d118d7f0.jpg[/img][/td] 
    [/tr]
[/table]

Check out these two Multi-Vehicle SAM Systems! First up is the Tan-SAM kai for Japan, capable of firing the Type 81C ARH with “Maddog” mode. Plus Germany’s IRS-T SLM that features the IRIS-T SL missile for engaging aircraft far away.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [td][h3]Tan-SAM kai[/h3][/td] 
        [td][h3]IRIS-T SLM[/h3][/td]

[h2]Multi-Vehicle SAM Systems[/h2]
Leviathans introduces a new type of vehicle called “Multi-Vehicle SAM Systems” and a new mechanic to control them! The following vehicles have new this new mechanic: 

[list]
[*] CLAWS (USA)
[*] IRIS-T SLM (Germany) 
[*] Tan-SAM kai (Japan)
[/list]

So how do these new vehicles work? You first spawn into a vehicle that has a radar and no weaponry whatsoever. This is the main “hub” vehicle if you will, that allows you to place launchers. To place launchers, use the keybind shown or press Alt on your keyboard and hover over the action panel and click the “Deploy launcher” button. You can then deploy launchers with missiles on them close by when they highlight green. 

Since there is now more than one vehicle, you can switch between them using the “Switch between the radar and launcher vehicles” button. You can fire the missiles from the launchers while controlling the radar vehicle after you’ve locked onto them. Check out the full description of how they work in our dedicated blog using the button below!

[h2][url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/236390/announcements/detail/547862446583316843 style=button]Learn more here[/url][/h2]

[h2]Radar Control Screen[/h2]
A new, dedicated screen has been added to SPAA vehicles! This screen brings together already existing displays while improving them. It also adds entirely new ones giving you a better representation of the vehicle’s sensors while allowing you to fire at targets. The exact configuration of this screen will depend on the capabilities of the vehicle you are using, so some elements may not be present on certain vehicles, but we will tell you about the most complete one. 

As you can see, this configuration has a Plan Position Indicator (PPI) in the middle of the screen. It shows a 360 degrees display with all contacts around you, but now all of them are enumerated and have different icons depending on their type. Missiles that you launch are also displayed on it and there is a map image in the background. Not only does it look visually pleasing, but it also has great functionality. You can switch between tracked targets by right-clicking (or tapping on console) on them, meaning it’s not just pretty, but functional as well. 

[previewyoutube="r1HuVc0JaC8;full"][/previewyoutube]

On the left, you’ve got your pretty standard sight view, and below that is a vertical view indicator, which shows azimuth and altitude of all located targets (enumerated as well). At the bottom-middle part of the screen just above the action bar are hints for controlling your radar and weaponry. On the right, there’s a table of all located targets with their parameters — azimuth, distance, altitude, velocity and type. A tracked target can also be selected by clicking on it in the list. This screen will come in handy for many SPAAs and help to immerse you even more. 

[h2]Interface Improvements[/h2]
We’ve improved several areas of the interface, below are some of the most important ones.

[h3]Action panel[/h3]
The action panel features important icons, from ammunition and FPE in ground battles, to the visual weapons selector in air battles. We’ve gone ahead and improved this part of the game, adding several new buttons. For example, in air battles there is now a button for the Multi-function menu, landing gear extend/retract that highlights when you’re near an airfield and have a lower speed than the max allowed for gear extension, hover mode, SAS mode, turning on seekers and firing air-to-air missiles and more. These new buttons can significantly help new players (and older players too!) who are starting out, as they reduce the dependency on remembering and setting up keybinds. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/409ad00bb9cd82e66a45dc6c966fdafe0294384e.jpg[/img]

[h3]Scoreboard[/h3] 
The scoreboard is a very important aspect of the game. We’ve improved some areas in this window: when you hover over the name of a player’s vehicle, it now shows that full vehicle’s stat card (as it would from the hangar), allowing you to check out its characteristics if you’re interested. Plus, you can right click vehicles and add them to your wishlist! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/4d3f5d4c6b5db99aa0dd6357d70245bef1feea05.jpg[/img]

Besides this, when you hover over a player’s name on the scoreboard, it shows their player background, icon, frame and title in all their glory, plus the full list of vehicles in the player’s current lineup, including their Battle Ratings. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/b7f85aeec2ae449942c100645e428f96ed48df68.jpg[/img]

Don’t worry, as in Realistic Battles, you won’t see the enemy’s lineup when hovering over an enemy’s name — you’ll just see their player background, icon, frame and title. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/bed548f38e5c6ac8ae1211d8e9fdebc5124e1015.jpg[/img]

[h3]Spawn screen[/h3]
A bad weather warning is now displayed in all missions with the ability to respawn on an airfield. The warning is shown on the statistics and spawn screen for all vehicle types in brackets next to the weather conditions of the mission. The following conditions are considered bad weather: Hazy, Low cloud cover, Fog, Rain, Storm. In bad weather, the Auto spawn point now changes from the Air point to Airfield, and an icon with a tooltip explaining the reason why the point has been changed appears in the name of the spawn point.

[h3]The all-new “Destroyed by” card[/h3]
When you’re destroyed by another player, it now shows a new “Destroyed by” card. This card shows the enemy’s profile background, icon, title and most importantly the vehicle that destroyed you, the name, type, rank, Battle Rating and ammunition used — all making it easier to visually identify. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/e2136e1e3b19df4427e4b61ccb8bf295509471e9.jpg[/img]

[h3]Player Profile[/h3]
The Player Profile has had some improvements. Specifically, the “Camouflages” tab has been updated, with nations and categories added to the left of the screen, and camouflages in the middle. Search bars have been added to the “Medals”, “Achievements”, “Camouflages”, “Decals” and “Collections” tabs, plus the total number of each type owned, making it easier than ever to find what you’re looking for.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/39f9a73d6fd7bb614d0f916f783e6d12ed290243.jpg[/img]

[h2]Fuel dumping[/h2]
Fuel dumping has been added to the game for one aircraft, the F-111! Bind the “Fuel dumping” key and press it in-game. A stream of fuel will be released from the nozzle at the back of the aircraft. It can be ignited when turning on your afterburner. This obviously creates a larger heat signature for missiles to track you, but does look kind of cool in return! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4649813/db3a73719d1fafa27b30dc32af5371330dc40ad1.jpg[/img]

[h3]Naval characteristics, physics and damage model:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]The mechanics of fire spreading inside the barbettes has been updated.[/b] The fire in the barbette (elevator fire) can still start because of a shell exploding inside it or spread from the main caliber turret being on fire. Previously the fire in the barbette originated in the center of the elevator and grew in size spreading equally up and down eventually resulting in the whole elevator being on fire. Now the fire can originate from any point of the elevator. So if the fire spread from the turret to the elevator, it will spread from the very top of the elevator to the very bottom to it, giving the player more time to react, however, if the shell hit the bottom of the elevator, the fire will start there giving the player little to no time for to react. The “Ammo Wetting” modification still works: it reduces the chances of detonation when the magazine receives fire damage. The probability of detonation is checked constantly while the fire affects the module. This fire spreading mechanic works only for the big crewed elevators of main caliber turrets. Other elevators that lack rooms and personnel can not be set on fire and don’t conduct the fire through themselves.
[*] [b]The calculation of the detonation force of ammunition magazines has been updated.[/b] The force of the explosion is now calculated based on the amount of explosive in the shells and charges. The less ammunition left in the stowage, the weaker their explosion will be, and the less destruction it will cause to the ship.
[*] [b]Changes have been made to the flooding and survivability systems.[/b] Issues in the formation of breaches from kinetic penetration of the sides and from rupture by an explosion have been fixed. Previously, a rupture by an explosion could not always leave a breach, while kinetic penetration even with small ammunition constantly activated damage control systems. Now, breaches from kinetic penetration only by the largest shells lead to water intake. A breach by an explosion now has the correct dimensions, depending on its strength. In addition, the time for patching breaches for Bluewater fleet ships has been changed. It was too short, even large holes could be fixed in 1-5 seconds. Now, depending on the size, they are patched from 5 to 20 seconds when talking about holes caused by shell explosions. The largest holes from torpedoes take longer to repair.
